note: Canonical golden vectors for the reverse/primary-name selector. The SAME cases pin two hand-written copies that MUST agree or the wallet union (Granus vs clarvis / UI) false-disagrees on reverse resolution: cairnx pickPrimaryName (src/primary.ts, consensus repo) and cairn primaryNameOf (public/trade/state.js, UI). This file is the single source of truth; cairn/test/primary-name.test.mjs reads it from the sibling checkout. addr/owner use the placeholders A, B, C, C_UPPER (resolved by each loader); a name with no addr field models a V23-cleared record (resolver set n.addr = undefined). expected is the primary .csd name for the query addr, or null. Selector contract: among names where owner === addr AND addr === self, not expired, not locked, pick lowest effectiveHeight then lowest (code-unit) claimId. As of the 2026-07-06 promotion the canonical selector is @inversealtruism/cairnx-core pickPrimaryName (csd-sdk packages/cairnx/src/primary.ts); the cairnx service src/primary.ts and cairn UI primaryNameOf are thin adapters over it. It lowercases the QUERY address defensively (records are canonical-lowercase on chain), so the earlier per-copy case nuance is gone and all consumers now agree by construction. All fixture STORED addrs (record owner/addr) are lowercase (production-realistic); C_UPPER is the same account as C written mixed-case, used ONLY as a query to pin that defensive lowercase.

cases.desc: owns it but points elsewhere (owner A, addr B) -> not primary
points at A but A is not the owner (owner B, addr A) -> no reverse-map spoofing
oldest self-pointing wins regardless of alpha/insertion order
expired/lapsed self-pointing is excluded; the live one wins
offer-locked self-pointing is excluded; the unlocked one wins
V23 BEFORE clear: oldest self-pointing is primary
V23 AFTER clear: the old primary's addr is cleared (no addr field) -> next-oldest promotes
all self-pointing names cleared (no addr) -> null
addr stored lowercased, query lowercased -> matches (case-folding invariant)
uppercase/mixed-case QUERY against lowercase-stored records -> query lowercased defensively, matches
